domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: The leave request an employee creates and acts on; its status and the signed-in user's role jointly determine which actions are available in the web app.

domain_entities.name: Employee (role awareness)
domain_entities.purpose: The signed-in user's identity and role, sourced from GET /employees/me, used to decide which leave actions to render. Never derived from decoding the JWT in the browser.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: The catalog of leave types selectable in the request-leave form; the chosen code is submitted with the request.

business_rules: Dates cross the wire as ISO strings, never Date objects; the web client serializes startDate/endDate as ISO strings and parses server responses back to strings for display. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest date fields (startDate, endDate, submittedAt, decidedAt, cancelledAt) appears, not only here]

requestedDays = endDate - startDate + 1 inclusive calendar days, whole-day UTC, no weekend/holiday exclusion — the single canonical derivation, never re-derived client-side. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest.requestedDays appears, not only here]
A leave request may be created only when endDate is not before startDate, both dates are present, and a leave type is chosen; these are validated client-side before any network call.

Action availability is a function of (request.status, actor.role, actor.id vs request.employeeId): submit and cancel are available only to the request's owner; approve and reject only to a manager (or admin); an action the user may not take must not be rendered at all. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest action availability appears, not only here]

The signed-in user's role comes exclusively from the employee profile (GET /employees/me); the JWT is never decoded in the browser to determine what to show. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Role awareness appears, not only here]
When the backend rejects a create/action, the API's own error message is surfaced to the user (e.g. insufficient balance), never replaced by a generic failure message.
After a successful action, the leave detail page reflects the new status without a manual reload.
domain_notes:
This feature is client-side only (web/) and introduces no new domain entities, lifecycle states, or business rules beyond the existing canonical model. The domain slice reuses the reconciled entities: LeaveRequest (lifecycle DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED/REJECTED, plus CANCELLED), Employee (ACTIVE/TERMINATED/ON_LEAVE, with role EMPLOYEE|MANAGER|ADMIN), and LeaveType (static catalog). The web app consumes these as read models and drives the existing backend workflow (create/submit/approve/reject/cancel) without changing the API contract.

Key domain facts the web layer must honor: (1) dates cross the wire as ISO strings, never Date objects; (2) requestedDays is the canonical inclusive calendar-day count (endDate - startDate + 1) and is never re-derived client-side; (3) action availability is a pure function of (request.status, actor.role, actor.id vs request.employeeId) — submit/cancel are owner-only, approve/reject are manager/admin-only, and unavailable actions are not rendered; (4) role awareness comes solely from GET /employees/me, never from decoding the JWT in the browser; (5) backend rejection messages (e.g. insufficient balance) are surfaced verbatim; (6) after a successful action the detail page reflects the new status without a manual reload.

Lifecycle states to fold into architectureMdUpdate (all pre-existing, none new): LeaveRequest DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED; Employee ACTIVE/TERMINATED/ON_LEAVE; LeaveType static (no lifecycle). No new states are introduced by this feature.
